claim: RestoredManga's RK fields carry default values no caller relies on
reason: Accurate that MangaRestorer.kt:71 is the only construction and passes every RK field, but the defaults on fields added to Mihon's own data class (RestoredManga.kt:21-35, inside an RK island) are the usual way to keep upstream's call shape compiling through a hand-merged sync. The failure scenario is a hypothetical future slip, not a defect in the current tree.

claim: The 'installed extension apps' rule is written twice, and the backup copy filters through the adult-source gate that the restore copy reads past
reason: The two unions differ on purpose. BlacklistedSources.kt:3-13 hides the stock E-Hentai app while the built-in equivalent is active, because the stock app shadows the built-in sources. Leaving it out of field 710 then means a restore does not offer to reinstall an app the gate exists to suppress. RestoreInstalls.kt:129 says explicitly that it reads past the gate, so an app hidden on the device counts as installed and is not offered either. Both outcomes match the gate's intent. The 'as the restore's check counts it' comment is about loaded versus not loaded, which both sides do agree on.

claim: BackupNovel.toNovelImpl restates manga's favoriteAt fallback rule inline with no shared kernel or pin
reason: The rule is pinned. BackupDatesConformanceTest is parameterized over both types (lines 50-57) and reads favoriteAt back through getMangaImpl (line 144) and toNovelImpl (line 216). Its UNKNOWN case (lines 56-57, 261-262) asserts that an unknown date restores as Manga.UNKNOWN_FAVORITE_AT on both sides. The novel comment at BackupNovel.kt:78 is not a 'twin of' marker, and manga's extra favoriteModifiedAt fallback (BackupManga.kt:93-97) is a SY-era field that BackupNovel lacks. Changing either side's unknown-date handling turns the conformance test red.

claim: The restore's carried next-update rule (device's, else the backup's) is written inline in both restorers with no kernel or test pinning it
reason: The device-else-backup choice is pinned. RestoreNextUpdateConformanceTest is parameterized over both types (EnumSource Type) and runs each type's real restore over real SQL (class KDoc, lines 36-40). Its case 'the device's own next update wins over the backup's' (lines 66-71) asserts device = now+2d beats backup = now+5d. If either `dbX.nextUpdate ?: x.nextUpdate` line flipped, that test would fail. The finder searched only RestoreMergeConformanceTest.

claim: Merge-group restore rule is pinned by a hand-maintained twin pair, not one conformance test
reason: The shared rule is pinned once, at the kernel, which is the rung testing.md prefers. RestoreMergeGroupsTest.kt has 15 tests over RestoreMergeGroups, including 'a group with fewer than two resolvable members is not created' (:264). The per-type tests in MangaMergeBackupRoundTripTest and NovelBackupRoundTripTest check each adapter's wiring (id resolution through its own repository), not a second copy of the rule. A future rule added to the kernel lands in the kernel test.

claim: The novel merge 'backup then restore' test never encodes the backup
reason: The novel merge group already goes over the wire in BackupStreamFramingTest.kt:69-93. It writes a BackupNovelMergeGroup with BackupNovelSourceRef refs at field 702, decodes it through Backup.serializer() and asserts refs.map { it.source }, so a serializer failure on the group or its refs fails there. PrefEraRestoreConformanceTest also encodes BackupNovelMergeGroup unmerges through restoreEncoded. A renumbered refs field would be symmetric between encode and decode in any round trip, so this test going over ProtoBuf would not catch it either.

claim: 'an unset Kitsu score stays unset' cannot fail under any change to the scale factor
reason: The test pins what its name says: an unset (0) Kitsu score restores as 0. It would catch an added offset or a floor, such as clamping to Kitsu's minimum of 2. Pinning the factor is not its job. The neighbouring tests do that (:14, :20 expect doubling, :8 and :26 expect it kept), and they would fail if the factor were dropped or swapped. A test that pins one property and relies on siblings for the others is not a defect.

claim: App settings restore writes plugin-scoped storage keys, sign-in storage included, bypassing the Source settings path
reason: This is deliberate. Commit dfd99a8d8 ('fix(backup): back up plugin settings with Source settings', in v0.4.0 and later) moved plugin storage from App settings to Source settings, and its body says 'older backups still restore them'. Backups made before that change carry plugin keys only in App settings, so AppPreferenceCarry has to keep writing them on an App settings restore or those settings are lost. A crafted backup with App settings on can already write the app store generally, so this adds no new reach.

claim: Restore writes local-volume rows and Loose files mode for any series, not only local ones
reason: The restore does skip the isLocal gate (MangaRestorer.kt:111-115, LocalVolumeBackup.kt:42-50, NovelRestorer.kt:123), but nothing bad follows from it. A backup the app wrote carries empty localVolumes and null volumePick/looseFiles for an online series, because the write side filters at LocalVolumeBackup.kt:24, so the restore writes nothing for those entries. A crafted backup can already reach these tables by setting the entry's source to the local id, so a source check on restore would protect nothing. The worst result is stray rows keyed by a URL that no screen reads, with no crash and no user-visible effect.

claim: A backup with App settings and Extension stores off carries only bare novel-source names, so restored novels from uninstalled plugins lose icon, language, site and image headers
reason: This is deliberate and matches Mihon. data-and-backup.md:71 records field 717 as each novel source's name only, 'the twin of Mihon's 101', and Mihon's own library-only backup also carries just a source name, so a manga from an uninstalled extension restores as a name-only stub. The writer's KDoc (RestoreInstalls.kt:219-221) says on purpose that the fuller seen-source record comes with App settings or Extension stores. backedUpNovelSources' KDoc (AppPreferenceCarry.kt:165-168) says the record is widened only from what App settings kept. Both ends agree with that documented design.

claim: Restored category-id include and exclude sets are merged into the device's sets, so one category can end up both included and excluded
reason: The merge is upstream's own semantics, carried over on purpose. Mihon's restoreCategoriesPreference unions into the live set with += over its update include/exclude and download include/exclude pairs (refs/mihon PreferenceRestorer.kt), so the same include-and-exclude conflict exists upstream. Reikai's RK comment (PreferenceRestorer.kt:~190-192 and the restoreCategoryList note) says outright that the shared registry extends that same merge to its own keys, 'merged into the live list like the sets'. This is inherited upstream shape applied consistently, not a Reikai regression.

claim: A malformed ln_reader_js_snippets value in a backup wipes the device's JavaScript snippet list, while every other malformed string key is written raw
reason: The claimed harm does not depend on the carry. Every restored string key, ln_reader_js_snippets without the carry included, replaces the device's value with the backup's, so the device's own list never survives a restore of that key either way. Without the carry, a malformed value is written raw, NovelSnippets.decode then reads it as an empty list, and the next save writes that emptiness back. The outcome matches what the carry produces directly, so the device's list is not lost any more than through the generic path the finding compares against (the CSS key ends up the same).

claim: Imported chapter order sorts page labels differently from LNReader's CAST(page AS INTEGER)
reason: The two orderings differ only for a page label that starts with digits and then has more text ('1.5', '2 Vol'). No LNReader plugin in refs/lnreader-plugins produces such a label. Numeric pages are String(pageNo) or page.toString() (ao3.ts:70, royalroad.ts:105, lncrawler.ts:457). bakaTsuki's text pages ('Volume N', 'Other', novel titles, bakaTsuki.ts:682,790,840) give 0 under both SQLite CAST and toIntOrNull()?:0, so those sort the same way too. LnReaderBackup.kt:216 therefore matches CAST(page AS INTEGER) (ChapterQueries.ts:579) for every page value a real backup carries. The chapterNumber claim describes how the value is carried and shows no wrong output.

claim: A backed-up reader font setting can name a user font whose bytes the backup silently left out, and restore records no error
reason: Leaving out an oversized font is the documented design. The KDoc at NovelFontManager.kt:147-149 says a file over BACKUP_FONT_CAP is left out, and docs/dev/subsystems/data-and-backup.md:75 sets field 721 to 'each file under 32 MB'. The finding asks for a new user-facing report of a documented limit. That is a missing feature, not a broken round trip. The read-failure drop (runCatching) is an I/O edge case with no realistic trigger shown.

claim: Restore keeps an existing different font of the same byte size and discards the backup's font while reporting success
reason: This is deliberate and documented. The restore() KDoc (NovelFontManager.kt:162) says 'One already here at the same size is left alone'. It uses the same equal-size identity rule as mirror() (:221-223). A different face with exactly the same byte count and the same file name is speculative, and the font on the device stays usable.

claim: The pre-restore warning names a missing novel source by a rule of its own, not the backedUpSourceName kernel the restore uses
reason: The two rules do different jobs, and the split matches the manga side, which Mihon set up. Manga's pre-restore dialog names a missing source through sourceManager.getOrStub, the device's record (BackupFileValidator.kt:58-66). Manga's error log uses the backup's own name, else the id: upstream BackupRestorer.kt:207 is `sourceMapping[it.source] ?: it.source.toString()`, which Reikai now spells backedUpSourceName. The novel validator line says it is 'Named as manga's are' (:75-79) and follows the same split: backup name, then the device record via nameOf. backedUpSourceName deliberately has no device fallback (BackupNovelSource.kt:14-18). So the disagreement between the dialog and the log is inherited parity on both types, not a rule restated twice. No defect.

claim: The rule for mapping a backup's category order to a device category id is written out three times in Reikai code, and the novel copy rebuilds its lookup twice for every novel restored
reason: The performance claim is wrong. Manga does not build the lookup once per batch: restoreMangaStream calls mangaRestorer.restore(listOf(it), ...) once per entry (BackupRestorer.kt restore lambda), so MangaRestorer.restore runs getCategories.await() for every manga too (MangaRestorer.kt:67). The 'N vs 2N' contrast is one small category query per entry against two, not a library-sized difference. The parity concern is already pinned. RestoreCategoryMatchConformanceTest maps an entry's category orders to device ids over both types, preferring the entry's own type's category when a universal one shares the name (test :53-77). ManualOrderBackupTest covers the mapping inside restoredManualOrder. What is left is three one-line lambdas inside Reikai restorers, which is at most a style nit.

claim: RestoredManga.manualOrder is an untyped Pair<Long, Long>, so every caller has to remember that it means (category id, position)
reason: No defect. Both consumers destructure the pair correctly as (categoryId, position) (NovelRestorer.kt:266-268, and RestoreRepositoryImpl per the finder). The failure scenario needs a hypothetical future caller. Adding a type for it is a speculative refactor that YAGNI in code-quality.md argues against, with no current bug to motivate it.

claim: The App settings restore path writes plugin-scoped keys, webview sign-ins included, with no scope or sensitivity check
reason: The behaviour the finding describes is intended and was shipped as such. Commit dfd99a8d8 says in its body that older backups still restore plugin settings, and the CHANGELOG entry that commit added states it to users: "Backups made before this update still bring them back with App settings." So pre-0.4.0 backups restoring plugin storage through the App path (AppPreferenceCarry.kt:121, whose else branch has no ln_storage or ireader_storage skip) is the documented design, not a contradiction of the Source settings toggle. The finding's own write-up calls it deliberate. The webview sign-in angle adds nothing new: the finding concedes that only a crafted backup could plant such a key, and the Source path (PreferenceRestorer.kt:79-85) already accepts any in-scope key from a crafted backup, so this path opens no new exposure.

claim: engine() failure path inlines engine retirement instead of calling retireEngine
reason: The inline teardown at LnPluginHost.kt:153-156 is deliberate and correct for its context, and the stated failure scenario does not hold. It runs on the slot's thread already, per the comment at :152 and the engine() KDoc's 'inside onThread'. Its close is a plain non-suspending runCatching { q.close() } followed by an unconditional executor.shutdown(), so a cancellation cannot interrupt it. retireEngine's NonCancellable + withContext(dispatcher) wrapping (:643-651) exists only to hop onto the confinement thread when the caller arrives cancelled from elsewhere, which this path never needs. The ordering is the same (close, then shutdown). No behaviour diverges, and calling a suspending hop to the thread it is already on would add nothing.

claim: The case-insensitive 'did the plugin set header X' lookup is written four times
reason: These are three different header names with three different purposes: the UA default, the XSRF echo and the cookie overlay (LnHostBridge.kt:66, 71, 79). Each is the standard case-insensitive HTTP header idiom in one line. NovelImageRequests.kt:170 reads the value over a different input map, not a yes/no check. No project rule is encoded here beyond HTTP's own case-insensitivity. code-quality.md says three similar lines beat a helper, and the finder names no user-visible failure today. The rule a shared helper would hold (equals ignoreCase) cannot drift in any meaningful way.

claim: QuickJsCreationTest runs one 16-thread race, so removing the creation lock may still pass
reason: The claim is that the test 'may still pass' when the lock is removed. That is true of any concurrency test and was not shown here. The test already does what a race test can: 16 threads released together by a latch, with the Cash and dokar paths interleaved (QuickJsCreationTest.kt:24-37). The failure scenario named, a new direct QuickJs.create call bypassing createQuickJs, is a whole-tree grep's job, not this test's. No evidence that the test passes under mutation in practice.

claim: The test that an LNReader WebView's headers 'come without waiting for the scan' asserts only an empty map
reason: The test at NovelImageRequestsTest.kt:186-189 is named for, and pins, one behaviour: webViewHeaders does not wait for the extension scan. scanDone=false makes loadedNovelExtensionsFlow a flow that never emits (test lines 282-283), so if webViewHeaders started waiting on the registry for a plugin id, runTest would hang and fail. The assertion is weak, as the finding says, but the test still catches the thing it claims to catch. The failure scenario (webViewHeaders throwing, or no longer calling pluginWebViewHeaders) is a coverage gap in other code, not a defect in this test. pluginWebViewHeaders itself is pinned by the tests at lines 192-213. What is actually untested is how webViewHeaders wires a plugin id into pluginWebViewHeaders, which would be a separate finding.

claim: The novel WebView header branch is written in two RK islands, the activity's and the view model's
reason: The cited lines do not exist: WebViewActivity.kt has 200 lines and WebViewViewModel.kt has 96. The real islands are WebViewActivity.kt:83-88 and WebViewViewModel.kt:60-65. Each is a four-line dispatch to one shared function, NovelImageRequests.webViewHeaders (NovelImageRequests.kt:116), so the rule already lives once in a kernel. The islands follow upstream's own twinned structure in these two files, as the code-quality carve-out for upstream shape allows. A fix to how a novel page's headers are chosen would land in NovelImageRequests and reach both callers, so the failure scenario does not hold.

claim: webContentsDebugging is a one-caller wrapper around a boolean OR
reason: The extraction exists so the rule can be tested. isDebugInspectorBuild needs a Context and BuildConfig, so the pure function is what lets the novel gate be pinned by a JVM test, and it carries the process-wide KDoc. Pulling a rule out into a testable pure function is not what the 'premature abstraction' rule targets, and nothing is duplicated. This is a style preference, not a defect.

claim: The release-build half of the gate, isDebugInspectorBuild, has no test
reason: isDebugInspectorBuild (WebViewDebugging.kt:8-9) is upstream's condition copied verbatim (refs/mihon WebViewScreenContent.kt:359-360, BuildConfig.DEBUG && FLAG_DEBUGGABLE). Upstream ships it untested, and inherited code keeps upstream's shape. The finding names no current defect, only a hypothetical future edit (&& to ||). Testing it would also take a BuildConfig/ApplicationInfo harness for a constant two-term expression. That is a speculative coverage wish, not a defect.

claim: Clearing the clearance cookie is written in three places, and FlareSolverr's copy skips the challenged host after a redirect
reason: The behaviour claim does not hold. On the serverAnswers path the bypass server forwards only cookiesSent(cookieJar, request), which reads jar.loadForRequest(request.url) (RequestCookies.kt:13-14, called from FlareSolverrClient.kt:359). It saves the solution's cookies under request.url (FlareSolverrClient.kt:398-399). So the redirect host's old clearance is never forwarded or consulted on this route, and clearing it would change nothing. COOKIE_NAMES is Mihon's own upstream shape (refs/mihon CloudflareInterceptor.kt:278), which inherited code keeps. TurnstileBench.kt:112 is a debug bench reached only from the debug settings row. What remains is a one-line remove call written three times, not a defect.

claim: Single-page versus spread dispatch (leftOf, readTo, turn) is copied verbatim into both novel viewports
reason: Each duplicated piece is a one-line `if (spreadHost != null) NovelSpreads.x(...) else <identity or NovelPaging.x>` dispatch. NovelTextViewport.kt:1724-1728 and 1745-1751 match NovelWebViewport.kt:693-697 and 793-798. The spread rule itself already lives once in the NovelSpreads and NovelPaging kernels that both renderers call, so only the null-host branch is repeated. The finder also concedes that TextViewportContractTest (app/src/androidTest/.../TextViewportContractTest.kt) pins the two renderers' shared behaviour, and that is a rung the content-layer ladder accepts. code-quality.md says three similar lines beat a premature helper. No rule is restated here, so this is not a finding.

claim: insert() works out the seam inline when seamAbove() already does it
reason: The seam rule is already one kernel: NovelSeam.between(...).drawn(setting). insert (954-958), seamAbove (801-805) and redrawSeams (562) each just call that kernel with the neighbours at hand, and none of them restates a formula. A future gap rule would go into NovelSeam.between and reach all three sites. Calling seamAbove from insert would only change where the list lookup happens and would make the seam depend on the order in which `held` is mutated. The claimed failure scenario (one copy changed but not the other) needs logic that does not exist at these call sites.

claim: BackupCreator.mangaOrNull restates GetManga.await(id), which the manga backup creator already uses for the same merge-group members
reason: The two helpers do different things. GetManga.await (domain GetManga.kt:16-22) catches every Exception, CancellationException included, and logs each miss at ERROR. mangaOrNull (BackupCreator.kt:345-346) uses runCatchingCancellable, so cancellation is rethrown and a cancelled backup job actually stops. Swapping in GetManga.await would make a cancelled backup keep running with the cancellation swallowed, and it would log an error for every stale merge-group id. Making GetManga adopt the cancellable catch would mean patching Mihon's own interactor outside an RK island, which is a separate decision. This is a two-line, documented RK-island choice with different semantics, not a restated rule. At most a style nit.

claim: 'Encode with the parser, then writeField' is restated at three sites instead of living in BackupProtoWriter
reason: The 'restated rule' is one expression, writeField(out, n, parser.encodeToByteArray(serializer, v)). It appears inline at BackupCreator.kt:299 and :317, and as a one-line private extension in LnReaderBackupConverter.kt:113-114. code-quality.md says three similar lines beat a helper, and adding an overload for a framing change nobody has asked for is speculative (YAGNI). The failure scenario is hypothetical, and BackupProtoWriter.writeField is already the one place framing lives, so a size guard added there would reach all three call sites anyway. Nothing here is a duplicated rule.

claim: The merge-group restore rule is pinned by a hand-maintained twin pair, and the two halves already cover different amounts
reason: The merge-group rule is not pinned by the twin pair. Both restorers delegate to the shared kernel RestoreMergeGroups (MangaMergeBackupRoundTripTest.kt:35 builds it directly), and the kernel has its own test, reikai/domain/merge/RestoreMergeGroupsTest.kt. That is the kernel rung of the pin-once ladder, so the twin tests are adapter wiring checks and not the pin the rule relies on. What remains true is a naming and coverage nit: the manga test is called RoundTrip but never runs BackupCreator.backupMangaMergeGroups. That function is private (BackupCreator.kt:337), and no test reaches it. This is a test-coverage gap, not the rule violation the finding states.

claim: The font-ordering restore test relies on a real 200 ms IO delay and appends to unsynchronized lists from worker threads
reason: The real-time delay is deliberate and documented (NovelFontRestoreTest.kt:31). The restore under test runs its reads on Dispatchers.IO, which virtual time cannot advance, and the 200 ms wait exists to surface a concurrent ordering: if the two steps overlapped, the instant mock font restore at :22-26 would append first. The failure scenario needs the font step to take more than 200 ms, but that step is a mock that returns immediately, so it cannot happen. When the steps run in order, as the code intends, coroutine resumption orders the list appends (happens-before), so there is no real data race on those lists.

claim: Restore picks an extension listing by its own rule, skipping ExtensionManager's EH gate and per-key grouping
reason: The claimed harm does not happen. The selection at RestoreInstalls.kt:46-47 does skip mapListings' blacklist filter (ExtensionManager.kt:699), but that filter only hides the listing in Browse. The shadowing it guards against is blocked separately. AndroidSourceManager.kt:132-136 drops every source in BLACKLISTED_EXT_SOURCES while built-in E-Hentai is on, whatever is installed. So a restored stock E-Hentai app installs but registers no sources and cannot shadow built-in EH. It also comes back only because the user's own backup listed it as installed, and it works again once built-in EH is turned off. The same-versionCode case across stores with different keys is a tie between two repos the user already trusts, so either listing is a valid install. The rule is also not the same rule written twice: mapListings keeps one listing per (pkgName, signingKey) for Browse, and the restore needs exactly one listing per package. Sharing that kernel would not answer the restore's question. At most a low-grade nit about the missing libVersion tie-break.

claim: The live store fetch plus signing-key check is written twice
reason: The two sites exist as cited: RestoreExtensionInstaller.kt:40-44 and RestoreInstalls.kt:202-203. A whole-tree grep finds `signingKey !=` only at these two lines. But the shared part is one `fetch(url).getOrNull()` plus one `!=` comparison, and the two sites do different work around it. readStore plans: it fetches the store, then lists its extensions and builds a BackupRepo carrying `live.signingKey`. addTrusted re-fetches at add time, because the store may have changed since the user approved it, then upserts or records a failure line with its own reason (unreachable or key changed). The key that addTrusted compares against comes from the approved repos, which the planning read built from `live.signingKey` after it had already matched the backup's key. So both checks compare against the same recorded key and cannot disagree today. code-quality.md's anti-default says three similar lines beat a helper used once. A `fetchIfSigned` helper would also fold the unreachable case and the key-changed case into one null, and addTrusted needs to tell those apart for its log. The failure scenario (one site starts accepting keyless stores or normalises case) is hypothetical: the finding names no planned change.

claim: writeManualOrder is a public top-level function with a single caller in its own file
reason: The claim that the function has a single caller is false. A whole-tree grep finds a second caller in app/src/test/java/reikai/data/backup/ManualOrderBackupTest.kt:41, which calls listOf(1L to entry).writeManualOrder(...) directly. Making it private would break that test. Being public is a deliberate test seam, and no project rule (code-quality.md, architecture.md) requires a top-level helper with one production caller to be private. The failure scenario is a hypothetical future caller, not a present defect. In production, both creators reach it only through writeCategories (ManualOrderBackup.kt:26), so the category orders are always written alongside it.

claim: PluginWebStorageTest mocks two final classes the app owns and waits five seconds of real time on a real IO scope
reason: The test follows an established project pattern, not a one-off violation. testAppScope() (a real IO scope) is the shared stand-in for @AppCoroutineScope in 63 test files. mockk<NovelSourceManager>/mockk<LnPluginHost> appears in 40 test files. The test exercises the app-scope launch that outlives viewModelScope, so a real scope is the point. verify(timeout = 5_000) polls and returns as soon as the call lands, so it waits 5 s only on failure. Flaking on CI is speculative.

claim: PluginWebStorage ViewModel test mocks the Reikai-owned final classes LnPluginHost and NovelSourceManager
reason: Cited lines 143-155 do not exist: PluginWebStorageTest.kt is 106 lines, and the model test is at 76-100. This repeats finding 2's rule complaint, and mocking these classes is the standard pattern (40 test files). The claim that the test 'proves only the call was made' is accurate, but it is a unit test of the ViewModel's hand-off: verify checks both arguments, and storeWebStorage's key-writing (LnPluginHost.kt:372-377) is a separate unit. That is a scope choice, not a defect in this test.

claim: Boolean names in Reikai-owned files skip the is/has/should/can prefix
reason: The four cited declarations exist as quoted (LnPluginHost.kt:111 `var rebuild = false`, NovelRequestHeaders.kt:34, WebViewDebugging.kt:16, KitsuBackupScoreScale.kt:21), and they do break the letter of the code-quality.md naming line. They are not a defect specific to these files, though. Across reikai/ in app and domain, 309 of 457 Boolean val/var declarations have no is/has/should/can prefix (148 do). So unprefixed booleans are the normal style in Reikai code, and these four are arbitrary samples of it. No hook or lint enforces the rule. Renaming them in isolation fixes nothing systemic, and a tree-wide rename is the standalone refactor sprint code-quality.md forbids; the convention gets applied when a file is next touched. There is no failure scenario beyond readability: `rebuild` carries a comment (LnPluginHost.kt:109) and is read only at :470. Not a reportable finding.

claim: A WebView renderer the system reclaims while the novel reader is in the background closes the whole reader
reason: This is intended behaviour, documented and matching upstream. The KDoc at NovelWebViewport.kt:401 says "A dead renderer closes the reader, as the in-app browser closes its page". RendererGone.kt:11-15 says it copies upstream's in-app browser handling. Mihon's own WebViewScreenContent.kt:167-175 also toasts and navigates up for every renderer death, whatever didCrash() says. The same helper serves the EH login and tracker login screens (EhLoginWebViewScreen.kt:89, TrackerLoginWebViewScreen.kt:90). Reloading after a memory kill instead would be a new feature, not a defect against a stated rule.

claim: WebView reader's in-chapter link click handler accepts script-made clicks and cancels the opening seek
reason: The harm described is already within reach of a chapter script, so the missing isTrusted check adds nothing. Commit 18b01f6fd guarded the touch listeners to stop scripts stepping chapters and marking them read, not to protect the reading position. The scroll listeners at reader.js:1851-1864 carry no trust check, and any scroll persists the position. With embedded JavaScript on, a script can already call window.scrollTo after ready and the new position is saved. A scripted .click() that ends the opening seek costs nothing beyond that, and it cannot step or mark a chapter.

claim: Tracker WebView sign-in check runs on the Activity's lifecycleScope, so closing the screen cancels a sign-in that already found its cookie
reason: The code is as described: TrackerWebViewLoginActivity.kt:83 launches the check on lifecycleScope, and runCatchingCancellable at :117 rethrows a cancellation. But the behaviour is intended and documented. docs/dev/subsystems/tracking.md:86 says a closed login screen leaves the site session alone, and the KDoc at TrackerWebViewLoginActivity.kt:124-128 also plans for the closed-screen case. Closing the screen in the middle of the check counts as the user cancelling: nothing half-written is stored, the cookies are kept, and opening the screen again signs in, as the finder itself says. Upstream's TrackLoginActivity (refs/mihon TrackLoginActivity.kt:30) runs its sign-in on lifecycleScope the same way. The screen is an Activity hosting a WebView, the same shape as Mihon's tracker login Activity and outside the Voyager Screen and ViewModel convention. Nothing is lost that the user did not ask to drop, so this is a style preference, not a defect.

claim: Eight of WebViewSeamPositionTest's fourteen cases exercise only test-written HTML and JS, and two accept either outcome, so none of the eight can catch a Reikai regression
reason: This is intended. The class KDoc (WebViewSeamPositionTest.kt:22-27) describes the class as the spike that measures where Chromium's anchoring holds. It logs under tag WebSeamSpike and points at novel-reader-rendering.md for what it decided. The region KDoc at :303-308 says outright that the synthetic cases measure Chromium and that the real-document cases are the ones that catch a regression. The 'either outcome' asserts at :259-264 are meant to characterise the browser, as their own comment explains. A test that measures the platform on purpose cannot be faulted for not measuring Reikai. The doc listing at novel-reader-rendering.md:153 is still true, because the class does contain real-document cases.

claim: Restoring the same reading sessions twice is not pinned against duplication
reason: The failure scenario does not hold. Duplicate sessions on a second restore can only come from losing UNIQUE(chapter_id, ended_at) (reading_session.sq:10,20). That same key is already pinned for both content types by data/src/test/java/reikai/data/readinglog/ReadingLogRepositoryTest.kt:58-66, 'the same session recorded twice is stored once', a test parameterized over MANGA and NOVELS. A schema change that drops the key turns that test red for both tables. The other way to break restoreManga/restoreNovel (reading_session.sq:59-69) is to drop OR IGNORE, and that makes the second restore throw on the unique key rather than double the sessions. So tests do not stay green in either case. A restore-twice case would at most be redundant coverage, not a missing pin.

claim: Tsundoku's category contentType at 8001 has a different default, unmirrored by the clash test
reason: The wire facts are right. Tsundoku declares @ProtoNumber(8001) contentType: Int = CONTENT_TYPE_ALL (refs/tsundoku BackupCategory.kt:15, Category.kt:19-21) and encodes with a plain ProtoBuf (AppModule.kt:130-131), so an 'all' category is written without field 8001, and Reikai reads that as MANGA (BackupCategory.kt:25). The failure scenario still does not happen. Reikai deliberately ignores Tsundoku's novel marker: RefAppBackupFieldClashTest.kt:41 mirrors isNovel at 8000, and the test at :100-124 asserts that Tsundoku's entry fields read as nothing in Reikai. So every entry in a Tsundoku backup restores as manga, and none of them could appear in the novel library whatever the category's content type. Restoring the category as manga-only is the outcome that matches its entries. Reikai also has no user-facing 'all' category type: CategoryContentType.UNIVERSAL = 0 is documented as the system uncategorized row (domain/.../CategoryContentType.kt:3-11), so there is no correct value Reikai could map Tsundoku's ALL to. That leaves an unpinned default with no user-visible defect behind it. The comment at BackupCategory.kt:24 ('for the same field') is loose about the differing default, which is a wording nit and not a defect.

claim: No test pins the dot boundary in isSameSite, the rule that keeps a source's login headers off other hosts
reason: The dot boundary is pinned. PluginWebStorageTest.kt:65-66 (`a host that only ends in the site's name is another site`) calls pluginSiteStorage("https://site.example", listOf("https://evilsite.example/" to OTHER_STORAGE)) and expects null. pluginSiteStorage (PluginWebStorage.kt:105-106) is just isSameSite(pageUrl, site). If line 76 became picture.endsWith(own), "evilsite.example".endsWith("site.example") would be true, the function would return OTHER_STORAGE, and the test would go red. The finder only searched SameSiteTest and NovelImageRequestsTest and missed this third test over the same function. Because the mutation turns a test red, the claim that a regression 'ships green' is false. Adding a header-level case would be nice but is a coverage preference, not a missing pin.

claim: Clear cookies on a plugin's details page or in its WebView leaves the plugin's saved site sign-in in place
reason: The code is as the finder describes: NovelPluginDetailsViewModel.kt:69-74 and WebViewViewModel.kt:88-93 only remove jar cookies, and forgetAllWebStorage is called only from SettingsAdvancedScreen.kt:249,266. It still does not hold up as a defect. (1) The per-site clears copy their references on purpose. The details page's KDoc says it works as an extension's page does, and an extension's page clears cookies only. LNReader's own WebView menu (refs/lnreader-main/src/screens/WebviewScreen/components/Menu.tsx:67-69) clears the WebView cache and never touches the stored localStorage or sessionStorage. Only its global Advanced Clear cookies (SettingsAdvancedScreen.tsx:28-31, CookieManager.clearAll plus store.clearAll) drops them, and Reikai matches that in the Advanced screen. The KDoc in PluginWebStorageClear.kt:9-13 describes that global action, not a promise about per-site clears. (2) In the WebView-menu case the suggested fix would not work. A cookie clear leaves the WebView's own localStorage in place, and the capture in WebViewScreen/WebViewActivity stores the page's storage again when the browser closes (LNReader saveData, WebviewScreen.tsx:65-90, does the same). Calling forgetWebStorage there would be undone at once. (3) Clearing cookies leaving localStorage alone is normal for a cookie action. Nothing in ln-plugin-host.md Decisions promises that a per-site cookie clear signs a plugin out. The most this could be is a feature request for a per-plugin 'forget site sign-in' action.

claim: A plugin installed from a new address after an uninstall inherits the old script's captured site sign-in
reason: The code is as described: stale URLs come from installed metadata (LnPluginInstaller.kt:159), forgetWebStorage runs only when that set is non-empty (161), and uninstall (398-416) clears only the URL and metadata records. But the outcome is documented design, not a missed case. docs/dev/subsystems/ln-plugin-host.md:52 says 'Uninstalling leaves the keys ... so a reinstall gets its settings and logins back', with no condition on which URL the reinstall comes from. The Decisions line at :98 says storage is keyed by plugin id on purpose: 'scoping by URL would split a plugin's settings between repos'. The forgetWebStorage rule at :52 covers only an install that replaces a plugin still installed from another URL. A reinstall after an uninstall is the separately ruled 'reinstall gets logins back' path. The doc does not tell a repo-B reinstall apart from a repo-A one, and the plugin's ordinary storage: keys get the same id-scoped carry-over. Changing this is a design question for the owner, not a defect in the shipped rule.

claim: A reused WebView fetch page keeps the Chrome client hints when its user agent turns non-Chrome or blank
reason: The code is as described: WebViewFetcher.kt:253-254 reuses a page and calls setUserAgent for any non-null agent, and WebViewUtil.kt:117 returns before touching the metadata when the agent has no Chrome/ token. The harm the finding claims does not follow from that, for two reasons. (1) Blank agents almost never reach this code. The fetch agent comes from request.header("User-Agent") (WebViewFetcher.kt:160) on the request CloudflareInterceptor gets. UserAgentInterceptor runs ahead of it (NetworkHelper.kt:48 vs :88) and fills in the default whenever the header is null or empty (UserAgentInterceptor.kt:13-17). The default is the user's preference (NetworkHelper.kt:101), Chrome unless the user blanks it. A blank agent at the reuse branch therefore needs the user to have cleared the default-UA setting and the same origin page to have seen a Chrome agent first. (2) For a non-Chrome agent, the reused page is no more inconsistent than a fresh page. A fresh page with a Firefox agent runs the same early return (WebViewFetcher.kt:266, WebViewUtil.kt:117). It keeps the stock Android WebView brand in Sec-CH-UA, which is just as wrong next to a Firefox User-Agent, since Firefox sends no client hints at all. That is upstream behaviour (refs/mihon WebViewUtil.kt:117, per the finder). The reuse path only changes which wrong brand appears, Google Chrome instead of Android WebView. It adds no new inconsistency that a bot check could score against Reikai specifically. What remains is a contrived corner (user-blanked default UA plus a same-origin page reused across agents), with no failure shown on a real path.

claim: With no isolated world, the solver takes `complete` from the page-world bridge without the origin filter the probe got
reason: The code is as the finder describes (CloudflareInterceptor.kt:70-76 checks no e.origin, :376 feeds the solve, :416-423 is a page-world JavascriptInterface; TurnstileSolver.kt:189-193 makes onEvent the only input with no isolated world; SolveMachine.kt:66-69 moves COMPLETE to Verified). But this is a ruled decision. docs/dev/subsystems/cloudflare.md Decisions says the probe runs in an isolated world and an old WebView gets an events-only solve rather than none, and also that `complete` is the primary acceptance signal. That premise still holds. The gap also cannot be closed the way the finding implies. An addJavascriptInterface bridge is callable from any frame and passes on no origin, so adding an origin check to listenerScript would not stop a direct mihon.postMessage('complete'). The only fix is to drop the events-only solve, which reverses the decision. The code already admits the bridge is forgeable (CloudflareInterceptor.kt:371 'on the fallback bridge any script on the page can send anything'). The only scripts on a Cloudflare interstitial are Cloudflare's own and the challenged site's, and the worst outcome is a 403 with no Open in WebView offered.

claim: A title or author search from a details page no longer goes back to the catalogue it was opened from
reason: This is a recorded, deliberate divergence. The finding says no Decision records it, but docs/dev/upstream-sync.md:84, under Deliberate divergences, says Mihon's performSearch reads navigator.items[size - 2] and Reikai's does not. It states that "a library search walks past any catalogue so it always lands on the library", that both details screens go through searchLibraryFromDetails, and that a sync should keep the walk. The RK island at MangaScreen.kt:336-340 matches that record. So dropping the search back into the catalogue is recorded in the place the project law names for divergences from upstream. A missing row in details.md or browse-and-sources.md does not make it an undocumented drop.

claim: Retry on a failed manga chapter in the queue's series sheet does nothing while the manga downloader is running
reason: The finding stops at the first function that seemed to agree with it. `startDownloadNow` calls `downloader.updateQueue`, and that does reset the row: `Downloader.updateQueue` sets `it.status = Download.State.QUEUE` on every download it keeps (Downloader.kt:928), the ERROR row included. It also runs inside `editQueue` (Downloader.kt:944-952), which pauses a running downloader and then calls `startLocked` again, and `startLocked` resets ERROR to QUEUE as well (Downloader.kt:212-214). The `startDownloads` early return at DownloadManager.kt:77 therefore does not matter, and the retried chapter is picked up on a busy downloader just as on the novel side.

claim: Queue sort no longer reorders across series: upstream's by-source sort was replaced by a within-series sort with no recorded decision
reason: Sorting only inside each series is a deliberate choice, not an accidental loss. The KDoc on `sortedWithinSeries` (DownloadQueueKernel.kt:190-193) says Sort is meant to keep the series in their current order and mean the same thing for both types. The queue is a list of per-series cards whose order the user drags and which is saved (downloads.md:15, :125). A Mihon-style sort across a whole source would interleave series against that saved card order. A missing line in the Decisions section of downloads.md is a docs gap, not a behaviour bug.

claim: README section heading is in Title Case, against the repo's sentence-case rule
reason: The finding rests on the claim that this heading is Reikai's own wording and not inherited. That is false. The same heading appears word for word at ../refs/komikku/README.md:131, and git log -S shows it arrived in ffc644e3e, 'docs: model README features and contributing on Komikku'. So the README section was deliberately modelled on Komikku and kept its upstream heading. Every other heading in README.md is already sentence case: lines 7, 9, 23, 33, 37, 127, 146 and 150. At most this is a cosmetic style nit on a borrowed heading, not wrong content, and with its main premise disproved it does not stand as stated.

claim: Off-path manifest carries journey narration and a dated audit note
reason: The off-path manifest is a dev record rather than a behaviour doc, and its other entries carry dates, SHAs and owner attributions as content (line 37 'owner, 2026-08-28'; lines 128-129 and 145 tell rename history so a sync can map each row to its upstream path). Line 160 explains why the SettingsReaderScreen row arrived late and what now catches the case, which is the provenance this record exists to keep. The date-and-history lint (SUBSYSTEM_HISTORY) covers docs/dev/subsystems/ only, and scripts/lint-docs.sh has no rule for this file. workflow.md:17's 'not the journey' rule is about behaviour descriptions in README/docs. At most line 11's 'used to be enforced' phrasing is a style nit, not a defect.

claim: Diagnosis step 2 sends every user to a Check for updates row that FOSS builds hide
reason: The premise is wrong. updaterEnabled reads BuildConfig.UPDATER_ENABLED, which is Config.enableUpdater (app/build.gradle.kts:61). gradle/build-logic/.../BuildConfig.kt:35-36 sets enableUpdater = distribution != LOCAL. FOSS is built with -Pdist=foss (release.yml:128), so it has the updater, and release and nightly use -Pdist=github (release.yml:81, nightly.yml:142). Only local builds without -Pdist hide the row, and no user receives one, so every distributed build shows Check for updates.

claim: With series merging off, re-adding one member of a stored group clears its siblings' hides
reason: By ruling: rejoining the library shows the whole stored group, with no exception for merging off, which also keeps a still-hidden sibling from swallowing the re-added entry when merging is turned back on; LibraryHiddenTest pins it.

claim: Hide and Unhide run one transaction per selected series, so a large selection rebuilds the library many times
reason: Bounded: SQLDelight's query flow keeps only the latest notification and the engine's hidden set is a distinctUntilChanged StateFlow, so rebuilds track write time over assembly time, not the selection size.

claim: A filter that only hidden series pass makes the library say every entry is hidden
reason: The partition runs on provider rows already filtered, so the message is literally true of the filtered view and its Hidden entries link works; commit 3b729f026f scoped it to no shown row left on purpose.

claim: Download queue cancel and cancel-all run on viewModelScope, so leaving the Downloads screen can cut them off
reason: The failure scenario cannot happen. viewModelScope uses Main.immediate, so `launch` at EntryDownloadQueueViewModel.kt:134 starts at once.

claim: Library pager leaks a preference collector and SharedPreferences listener into the engine scope every time a page composes
reason: Half the claim is false. On the single-list path, `columns` and `displayMode` are remembered at LibraryTab.kt:649-650, outside `key(libraryContentType)` (opened at 657), so a chip flip does not rebuild them, and the comment at 646-648 is accurate.

claim: Follows screen restates the shared catalogue chrome and goes around its own adapter to the bulk model
reason: The owner has ruled on this. browse-and-sources.md:177 (Decisions) says 'MangaDexFollowsScreen keeps its own chrome', and parked.md:23 parks 'Fold the follows screen into the shared catalogue' as the one browse screen drawing its own chrome and dispatching off the manga model.

claim: Batch add hands the Activity context from LocalContext into a ViewModel coroutine that outlives rotation
reason: The code is real, but it is Komikku's shape kept almost line for line, and the parts that matter are intended. Komikku's BatchAddScreenModel.kt:33-105 and BatchAddScreen.kt:50,94 do the same thing: they take LocalContext.current, pass it to addGalleries(context) and loop on screenModelScope.launch(Dispatchers.IO + handler).

claim: The download queue scans the whole manga queue for every card on every progress sample to name its current chapter
reason: The premise that the scan runs once per card is false. withChapterName returns right away when currentChapterId is null (EntryDownloadQueueViewModel.kt:174), and toCards sets currentChapterId only for series in activeSeries (DownloadQueueKernel.kt:91-98).

claim: Files that arrive by event are lost on process death because only initialUris are saved
reason: This is documented behaviour. docs/dev/subsystems/local-novels.md:41 says files handed over are restored as route arguments, while 'files shared in later are events and never restored'.

claim: The Settings > Browse Repos count uses its own visibility rule, so it disagrees with the Repos screen it opens
reason: The mismatch is real. SettingsBrowseScreen.kt:66-71 and :98 count every extension store plus the plugin repos, and only gate on whether novels are shown, while RepositoriesViewModel.kt:66-67 filters through shownIn (RepoCards.kt:40-41).

claim: LibraryEngine restates EntryId.of inline with the opposite fallback for ContentType.ALL
reason: The failure scenario cannot happen. Every ManualOrderPosition comes from LibraryManualOrderRepositoryImpl.kt:70 via Long.toContentType() (ContentTypeColumn.kt:16-20), which returns only MANGA or NOVELS and errors on anything else, or from the restorers (NovelRestorer.kt:262, RestoreRepositoryImpl.kt:89), which pass MANGA or NOVELS explicitly.

claim: Write-aside-then-rename for app-private files is hand-rolled in three Reikai-owned files
reason: The three sites are a short, idiomatic write-aside-and-rename pattern, and they differ in input and failure contract, so they are not one rule restated. LocalNovelSource.kt:397-411 returns early when the target already exists, takes bytes from a lazy producer, then deletes the book's older copies.

claim: LibraryHiddenRepository keys a hide by (ContentType, raw Long), so the type can be ALL and every impl method carries an error branch for it
reason: The suggested EntryId shape cannot be expressed at this boundary. EntryId lives only in :app (app/src/main/java/reikai/domain/entry/EntryId.kt, the only copy a whole-tree search found), while LibraryHiddenRepository sits in :domain (domain/src/main/java/reikai/domain/library/LibraryHiddenRepository.kt:10) and its impl in :data (LibraryHiddenRepositoryImpl.kt:19).

claim: About a third of the dup baseline is DI constructor lists, so the DRY guard re-fires on every constructor edit and trains authors to rebaseline
reason: Keeping these clones is a choice the project documents, not an accident. The baseline header (scripts/dup-baseline.txt:11-13) keeps constructor parameter lists naming the same repositories, with no logic shared, as a named pair group.

claim: Skill's fix and scope rules leave out the write-once rule for manga and novels
reason: The omission is real, but it does not lead to the failure scenario. content-layer.md loads every session (CLAUDE.md says so), so the write-once rule is already in force for any agent running the skill.

claim: The guess-tier rule that a page must name an entry and have something to read is restated in both resolvers and pinned by drifting twin tests
reason: The two guess bars are not the same rule. ResolveNovelLink.isANovel (line 121) uses sentName, which rejects plugin placeholder names such as Untitled (tested at 258-268), and it accepts a paged novel with no first-page chapters (totalPages > 1, tested at 229-238).

claim: Combine re-keys a manga series' per-file and lent loose volume rows (notes, label, order) to keys the kept series never reads
reason: The re-keying happens as cited (CombineLocalVolumes.kt:172-175 uses localGroupKey, LocalGroups.kt:89-90, while A reads B's loose chapters through localVolumeKey, LocalGroups.kt:97-98, which applies Each its own only to the owner's own folder). But hiding them is the documented rule, not a defect.

claim: A selector write still running after the user removes the tracker puts the binding back
reason: The mechanism checks out: manga_track.sq:59-79 upserts on (manga_id, tracker_id) and ignores the row id, and pushTrackEdit (PushTrackEdit.kt:21-22) persists after a network update. But this is upstream's shape exactly.

claim: A field edit from a stale snapshot pushes old progress to the service, bypassing the forward-only push rule
reason: Status, score and date edits do send the snapshot's last_chapter_read through tracker.update (PushTrackEdit.kt:22, ServerProgress.kt:11-12). But the forward-only rule cited in tracking.md:99 covers chapter pushes from reading, which go through the chapter-push path (ChapterPushOutcome, ForwardOnlyPushConformanceTest), not field edits.

claim: The versionCode comment restates the line below it and repeats a CLAUDE.md fact that changes every cycle
reason: Owner ruling: leave as is. app/build.gradle.kts:52-55 carries real WHY (versionCode climbs mid-cycle because a migration is a no-op below its gate) and its cycle numbers (205, 210, next 211+) match current code (line 56) and CLAUDE.md.

claim: ClearDatabaseSectionHeader adds a new list header where Mihon's shared ListGroupHeader exists
reason: Owner ruling: leave as is. ClearDatabaseScreen.kt:270 draws primary labelMedium; ListGroupHeader.kt:12 draws onSurfaceVariant SemiBold bodyMedium, so it is not an equivalent and swapping changes the look.

claim: The fonts screen resolves a reader font to a face again, beside the reader's cached resolver
reason: Owner ruling: leave as is. The shared rule is the classification readerFontSource (NovelFont.kt:82), which both NovelFontsScreen.kt:184 and NovelTextStyle.kt:109 call.

claim: NovelDeleteDialog and SavedSearchDeleteDialog are the same Reikai-owned confirmation dialog
reason: Owner ruling: leave as is. SavedSearchDialogs.kt:76 is ported from Komikku's BrowseSourceDialogs.kt:57 and keeps that shape (Delete confirm label, dismiss after delete); NovelToggleList.kt:171 confirms with OK and leaves dismissal to the model.

claim: The restore error's RK island pastes upstream's section block three more times
reason: Owner ruling: leave as is. RestoreBackupScreen.kt:141-174 repeats upstream's own bold-title plus joinTo block (refs/mihon f64d82b94 same function, sources and trackers) three times inside the RK island.

claim: cancelNovelLibraryUpdatePendingBroadcast restates novelDownloaderPendingBroadcast line for line
reason: Owner ruling: leave as is. NotificationReceiver.kt:617-628 does equal novelDownloaderPendingBroadcast(context, ACTION_CANCEL_NOVEL_LIBRARY_UPDATE) (:603), but it copies the per-action shape upstream repeats (cancelLibraryUpdatePendingBroadcast :544, the download broadcasts :312-360), sits far below the dup-check threshold, carries no rule that could drift, and predates the range (blame 2026-06-14).

claim: The rule for telling a manga source from a novel app's source is written out separately at each call site
reason: Owner ruling: leave as is. The rule exists once, Extension.Kind.novelSourceId (reikai/novel/source/NovelSource.kt:23).

claim: The 'Statistics is a bottom-bar tab' check is written inline twice, beside a kernel that covers only the menus case
reason: Owner ruling: leave as is. The two inline checks (MoreTab.kt:96 statsShortcut != StatsShortcut.TAB, HomeScreen.kt:155-156 == StatsShortcut.TAB) are a single enum comparison, the setting's own value read through different plumbing (asState vs collectAsState).

claim: forgetAllWebStorage makes every caller pass in the PreferenceStore that LnPluginHost already holds
reason: Owner ruling: leave as is. LnPluginHost.kt:70-84 takes preferenceStore as a plain constructor parameter handed to LnHostBridge; it is not a property, so the extension at PluginWebStorageClear.kt:21 cannot reach it.

claim: Which route counts as an overlay is written twice: the sheet metadata and a hard-coded type check in shownRoute
reason: Owner ruling: leave as is. ShownRoute.kt:9 excludes EntryTrackSheetRoute by type; ReikaiNavGraph.kt:110 is the only overlaySheet() entry.

claim: The novel selection-key formula from a SelectedNovel is restated at two sites instead of one helper
reason: Owner ruling: leave as is. The key formula lives once, novelRowKey at EntryBrowseRows.kt:30.

claim: RepositoriesTitle copies Mihon's title-plus-count pill a fourth time
reason: Owner ruling: leave as is. RepositoriesTitle (RepositoriesScreen.kt:187-205) is the title plus count pill idiom that upstream itself writes inline three times (refs/mihon LibraryToolbar.kt:74, DownloadQueueScreen.kt:94, Tabs.kt:15).

claim: openDetails goes through the per-type payload when every caller but PickMember already holds an EntryId that detailsRoute takes
reason: Owner ruling: leave as is. MigrationEntry and MigrationFavorite (MigrationFlowAdapter.kt:136-141) do carry an EntryId, but pushDetails (MigrationCandidateUi.kt:26-31) derives the same id from the payload both are built from, so the two cannot disagree, and PickMember (Long id, MigrationSourcePick.kt:26) still needs the payload branch.

claim: The prioritize-by-chapters probe hand-rolls the per-source fan-out that fanOutPerSource already encodes
